description: Every script in this repository that an agent or a person may run. The safety class is one of read-only, local-write, remote-write, or human-only. An agent never runs a human-only entry. A later MCP server lists only the tools whose mcp_exposure is expose.

mcp_exposure.expose: The MCP server lists the tool.
mcp_exposure.hidden: The MCP server never lists the tool. This is the default when the field is missing, so a new tool stays out of the server until someone marks it. A human-only tool must be hidden.

tools.name: gates
tools.description: Run typecheck, lint, test, build, and check:pack in order. Record the real exit code of each. Print one line per gate.

arguments.name: --ci
arguments.description: Run npm ci first.

arguments.name: --bail
arguments.description: Stop at the first failing gate.

arguments.name: --cwd
arguments.description: A folder inside a git work tree. Default: the current folder.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, status, exit, path, gates: [{ name, command, exit, signal, ok, firstFailingLine? }] }. Exit 0 all passed, 1 a gate failed, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: node_modules (with --ci) and dist, in the folder.

tools.name: pr-open
tools.description: Check the pull request body, then open a DRAFT pull request with gh. It never opens a ready pull request.

arguments.name: --title
arguments.description: One line, at most 256 characters.

arguments.name: --body-file
arguments.description: A regular file of at most 64 KB.

arguments.name: --base
arguments.description: The branch to merge into.

arguments.name: --dir
arguments.description: A folder inside a git work tree. Default: the current folder.

arguments.name: --dry-run
arguments.description: Check the body and print the command. Do not call gh.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, status ("pass" | "dry-run" | "invalid-body" | "gh-failed" | "usage"), exit, draft, command, url } or { problems: [...] } for an invalid body. Exit 0 opened, 1 body or gh failed, 2 wrong use.
tools.writes: Opens a draft pull request on GitHub. It writes no local file.

tools.name: tree-clean
tools.description: Report whether a clone tree is clean, pushed, and idle. It removes nothing. Removal belongs to the factory-tree finish step.

arguments.name: <tree>
arguments.description: The top folder of a git work tree.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, status, exit, path, removes: "nothing", checks: [{ name: "clean" | "pushed" | "idle", ok, detail }] }. Exit 0 all pass, 1 a check failed, 2 wrong use.

tools.name: release status
tools.description: Read the version, the git tags, and the registry. List what is left to do. Reads the network with a throwaway home folder and cache.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { package, version, phases: [{ name, state }], left: [...] }.
tools.writes: Network reads only. It changes nothing in the repository and nothing in the home folder.

tools.name: release preflight
tools.description: Phase 1. Check the checkout is the release branch, up to date with the remote, and clean. Record the commit hash.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is already done.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { commit }.
tools.writes: Runs git fetch, which updates FETCH_HEAD and the remote-tracking refs inside .git. Writes release-state.json inside .git.

tools.name: release gates
tools.description: Phase 2. Run npm ci, typecheck, lint, test, build, and check:pack. Stop at the first failure.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is already done.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { commit, failingLine? }.
tools.writes: node_modules (npm ci) and dist (build) in the working tree, and release-state.json inside .git.

tools.name: release dry-run
tools.description: Phase 3. Run npm publish --dry-run. Check the package name and version, the file count, the size, and the tag.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is already done.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { commit, failingLine? }.
tools.writes: dist in the working tree (the dry run repeats the gates) and release-state.json inside .git. Nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: release publish
tools.description: Phase 4. Print the commands for a person to publish. Never runs them. Refuses without a terminal.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { commands: [...] }.
tools.writes: Nothing. It never runs npm publish or npm login.

tools.name: release verify
tools.description: Phase 5. Read the dist-tags and install the package into a clean temporary project. Count the exported names against the public API list.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

arguments.name: --force
arguments.description: Run the step again even if it is already done.

arguments.name: --allow-unsandboxed
arguments.description: Import the installed package without the Node permission model when this Node lacks it. Without the flag, verify stops with exit 1.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { commit, exports }.
tools.writes: A temporary project folder outside the repository (removed afterward), the npm cache, and release-state.json inside .git.

tools.name: release tag
tools.description: Phase 6. Tag the commit that preflight saw and push the tag. Refuses unless verify passed and the tree is clean.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

arguments.name: --dry-run
arguments.description: Print the git commands and run none of them.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { tag, commit, commands? }.
tools.writes: A git tag in .git and the same tag pushed to the remote.

tools.name: release retire
tools.description: Phase 7. Print the commands that retire the old version. Never runs them. Refuses without a terminal.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { commands: [...] }.
tools.writes: Nothing. It never runs npm deprecate or npm dist-tag.

tools.name: release claims
tools.description: Phase 8. Search README.md and the docs for text that says the package is not published.

arguments.name: --json
arguments.description: Print one JSON object instead of text.

tools.output: { ok, command, status ("pass" | "fail" | "already-done" | "refused" | "usage"), exit, message, steps: [{ command, exit }] } plus { failingLine? }.
